## Files Reviewed - `src/pages/cv/index.astro` — full file (frontmatter + markup), plus diff vs HEAD - `src/lib/structured-data.ts` — JSON-LD helper conventions - `src/pages/blog/[slug].astro` — `` component pattern (astro:assets) for comparison - `public/images/coursera-golang.png`, `coursera-cybersecurity.png` — both 1650×1275 (4:3), ~715KB each ## Critical (must fix) - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:118-135` — Cert date "August 5, 2026" is **today** (current date verified via `date`: Aug 5, 2026) and July 19, 2026 is in the past. Certificates dated within days/weeks of a public CV page look fabricated. Suggest using `completedDate`/`issuedOn` in the array and displaying it as "Issued August 5, 2026" or similar, or holding the post until dates are genuinely true. The JSON-LD mirrors this at lines 43-46 / 56-59 (`dateCreated: "2026-08-05"` / `"2026-07-19"`). If these dates are accurate, fine — flagging for verification. - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:275-277` — `alt={cert.title}` duplicates the visible `

` heading text below. Screen readers will read the same title twice and the image (a Coursera certificate screenshot) conveys no info beyond the heading. Use a short functional alt (e.g. "Coursera certificate for {cert.title}") or `alt=""` with `aria-hidden` since the title follows immediately. At minimum, avoid exact duplication. - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:275` — **Missing `decoding="async"`** on ``. Project convention: blog images (`src/pages/blog/[slug].astro:264-272`) always set `decoding="async"`. Also missing `width`/`height` attributes — the 1650×1275 images are 715KB each (1.4MB total); without dimensions, layout shift occurs on load (CLS). At minimum add `width="1650" height="1275"` (or `width={…} height={…}` computed in the array) so the browser reserves space and `loading="lazy"` works properly. ## Warnings (should fix) - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:277` — `max-w-md w-full` caps the image at 448px while the card is up to ~672px wide (max-w-5xl container minus padding). Card is then taller than it needs to be and the image floats left-ish with empty space to its right. On 4:3 ratio that's a 346px-tall image in a 672px-wide card — awkward. Suggest either: (a) full card width with `rounded-lg`, or (b) a 2-col layout (image left, text right) on md+ screens — the latter matches the site's grid-based section patterns and halves the vertical footprint. - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:118-135` — Duplication: cert data appears twice (array at 118-135 and JSON-LD at 40-67) with hand-maintained fields. The site already derives JSON-LD from source data elsewhere (e.g. `buildHomePageSchemas(projects)` in `structured-data.ts`). Consider generating `hasCredential` from the `certifications` array (a `buildResumeSchema(certs)` helper) so one edit updates both — especially important since titles are long and easy to typo. - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:275-277` — Plain `` + 715KB PNG. Project already uses the `Image` component from `astro:assets` for blog images (optimizes, resizes, sets dims). If this is the CV page's only image content, acceptable; but converting to `Image` (or at least pre-optimizing to webp/avif via `astro:assets`) would cut weight significantly. Suggest adding `src` imports to `src/content/` or `public/images/` so Astro optimizes at build. ## Suggestions (consider) - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:290` — "Verify on Coursera →" — the arrow char (`→`) appears only here in the entire codebase (checked `src/pages` + `src/components`). Other CTA links use inline SVG icons + `gap-2` styling. For consistency, either drop the arrow or use an icon like the hero CTAs. Minor. - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:290` — Missing `aria-label` for external link; target="_blank" + rel="noopener noreferrer" is correct (matches CTA section pattern at 312/320). Add `aria-label="Verify {cert.title} on Coursera"` for a11y precision if you keep the generic "Verify on Coursera" text. - `src/pages/cv/index.astro:286-291` — Could use `transition-colors hover:text-accent` on the link to match other hover behaviors on the page (hero CTAs all have hover states). - Date ordering: certs listed Golang-first but JSON-LD also Golang-first; chronological (Cyber first) would be more natural if intended as timeline. Consistency between display order and schema order is correct as-is, so just a preference note. - `public/images/coursera-*.png` — both 1650×1275, no alt-text info inside; confirm screenshots don't contain sensitive data (they're public in `/public`). ## Design Consistency Rating **Good — matches.** The section follows the exact established pattern: `mb-12` section spacing, `mb-6 text-2xl font-bold` heading, `rounded-xl border border-border bg-surface/50 p-6` cards (matches technicalStack/coreProjects/experience), `hover:border-accent/50` (matches coreProjects), mono uppercase tracking accent label for issuer (matches technicalStack category labels and hero eyebrow). Card layout (`space-y-4` stacked full-width) matches experience section exactly. The only deviation is the image insertion, which is a new element type for this page — handled reasonably but has the sizing/CLS issues above. ## Correctness - Both Coursera links verified live: HTTP 200 (`coursera.org/share/54e2aa035e749894bbed3095fd72dae7`, `2ff823307adc11d32da031d966fd98d1`). - `target="_blank"` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` correct (noopener is redundant with noreferrer but harmless). - JSON-LD: `EducationalOccupationalCredential` with `credentialCategory: "course"`, `offeredBy` Organization, `dateCreated`, `name`, `url` — schema.org-valid structure. Data matches the visible array 1:1 (verified programmatically). - Images exist on disk, referenced paths correct. ## Summary Section is structurally clean and visually consistent with the page — the builder nailed the card/heading/spacing conventions. The real issues are image handling (missing width/height + decoding → CLS risk on 715KB images; `max-w-md` creates awkward card layout) and the date plausibility question. Recommend fixing image dims/alt, and reconsidering the "issued today" date before this ships. Duplication between the array and JSON-LD is worth refactoring eventually but is not blocking.
